  • Infrastructure Architecture (IA) owns the design, security, and evolution of Salesforce's first-party data center network. We architect the routing, switching, firewall, and load-balancing infrastructure behind large-scale sites that span several Salesforce business units. We also own the backbone connectivity to the internet and to our public cloud environments (AWS and GCP). As a Principal Network Engineer, you will set technical direction for this network and lead the security posture of our edge. You will also manage the lifecycle of the hardware and designs behind it.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Define and evolve reference architectures for first-party data center networks. These span routers, switches, firewalls, and load balancers, with lighter touchpoints into compute.
  • Design network and application delivery architectures for large-scale sites that serve multiple business units across Salesforce.
  • Own backbone and internet connectivity, plus interconnect between our data centers and public cloud environments (AWS and GCP).
  • Own infrastructure lifecycle for hardware and designs. For example, you might lead a refresh of an aging top-of-rack switch by evaluating and selecting a suitable newer model, then defining the validated design and transition approach.
  • Build and maintain network automation and tooling in Ansible and Python, managed in Git repositories. Use AI models in day-to-day design, development, analysis, and documentation work.
  • Act as a technical authority and escalation point for complex design, capacity, and incident-driven architecture questions.
  • Lead network security architecture, including security feature design and edge hardening. Partner with Network Operations, Security, Supply Chain/Capacity Planning, and cloud teams to deliver at scale. Mentor engineers and influence cross-org technical strategy through design reviews and architectural documentation.
  • Drive deployment and tuning of edge protocols and policy, such as mTLS, HTTP/2, and cipher suite changes.
  • Run software certification and vulnerability and bug management for network platforms, coordinating remediation with vendors and operations teams.

You're Our Person If You Have:


  • 10+ years of experience in network engineering or architecture, with a track record at data center or service-provider scale. Software-driven engineering skills: Ansible, Python, and Git-based development workflows. Vendor familiarity with Cisco, F5, Juniper, and Ciena.
  • Familiarity with liquid cooling and high-density facility considerations (such as direct-to-chip cooling, power and thermal constraints, and rack density) and how they influence network hardware selection, rack layout, and design.
  • AI fluency: hands-on experience and familiarity with AI models, and the ability to apply them effectively in engineering workflows.
  • Proven record of leading multi-team, multi-year architecture efforts.
  • Deep expertise in large-scale data center and WAN/backbone design (BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, L2/L3 fabrics, routing policy). Load balancing and application delivery design experience, particularly with F5 (BIG-IP). This includes certificate management and lifecycle, and how certificates and keys are assigned to virtual servers; SSL/TLS termination and re-encryption design, including client-SSL and server-SSL profiles; SSL and HTTP header handling, such as forwarded client IP and protocol headers; and traffic policy and customization through iRules and related profiles (HTTP, persistence, and others).
  • Hands-on experience with firewalls and TLS termination at the edge.
    Strong security background: vulnerability management, software qualification, and secure protocol configuration. Experience with hardware lifecycle planning, including platform evaluation, refresh, and migration.
  • Experience with new GPU cluster builds, including topology planning, capacity and scale modeling, and coordination with compute, storage, and facilities teams from design through deployment.
  • Clear communication with executives and engineers.

Even Better If you have:

  • Vendor familiarity with Cisco, F5, Juniper, and Ciena.
  • Familiarity with public cloud connectivity (AWS Direct Connect, GCP Interconnect) and hybrid architectures. Knowledge of AI data center network design, including high-bandwidth, low-latency fabrics for GPU clusters (for example InfiniBand or RoCE/Ethernet-based back-end networks) and the front-end/back-end network separation typical of AI workloads.
  • Familiarity with liquid cooling and high-density facility considerations (such as direct-to-chip cooling, power and thermal constraints, and rack density) and how they influence network hardware selection, rack layout, and design.

We are looking for a seasoned Security Practices Director with strong Application Security (AppSec) credentials to join our Professional Services team, leading security and compliance engagements that help customers maximize the value of their Salesforce investments — safely and at scale. This role is primarily an AppSec expertise role; prior consulting/engagement management experience is a plus but not required — we'll support your growth into the client delivery and engagement-management aspects of the role.


What You'll Do

  • Apply AppSec expertise (secure SDLC, vulnerability assessment, threat modeling, pen-test interpretation) to lead and validate technical security engagements for enterprise customers
  • Identify and advise on common application vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10, injection, broken access control, SSRF, insecure deserialization, etc.)
  • Advise customers on how to securely implement and use SaaS platforms day-to-day — configuration hardening, access/identity management (SSO, MFA, OAuth), integration and API security, data protection, and ongoing operational security hygiene across the SaaS lifecycle
  • Translate AppSec findings into prioritized, risk-based remediation roadmaps for client stakeholders
  • Lead end-to-end delivery of security engagements — scoping, staffing, timeline, and risk ownership
  • Partner with account teams and sales leadership on pre-sales — discovery, solution scoping, SOW development, and executive presentations
  • Act as trusted advisor to C-suite and senior security stakeholders (CISO, CTO, VP of IT Security), translating technical risk into business terms
  • Oversee delivery teams to ensure consistent methodology and quality across engagements
  • Develop reusable delivery accelerators, methodologies, and playbooks grounded in AppSec best practice
  • Mentor practice staff on both security substance and client-facing engagement skills

What We're Looking For

  • 7–12+ years of AppSec experience (secure SDLC, vulnerability management, threat modeling, pen testing) — core, hands-on requirement
  • Deep, working knowledge of the OWASP Top 10 and common application-layer vulnerability classes, and how to assess/mitigate them in practice
  • Practical understanding of how to secure a SaaS platform through implementation and ongoing use — configuration hardening, IAM, API/integration security, and the shared-responsibility model, not just theoretical SaaS architecture
  • Strong executive communication and presence; comfortable with CISO/CTO-level conversations
  • Security certifications strongly preferred (CISSP, OSCP, or equivalent AppSec certs)

Nice to Have

株式会社セールスフォース・ジャパンは、Great Place To Work® Institute Japan（GPTW）が発表した2026年版「働きがいのある会社」女性ランキングにおいて第2位に初ランクイン、また大規模部門（1,000人以上）においても第3位に選出されました。
弊社では「Equality（平等）」をコアバリューの一つとして掲げ、性別やライフステージに関わらず、すべての社員が能力を最大限に発揮できるインクルーシブな環境づくりを推進しています。社内コミュニティ「Salesforce Women’s Network（SWN）」をはじめとするネットワーキングやキャリア形成支援、メンターシップ制度も活発に稼働しています。

【働き方・ワークライフバランスの推進】


ハイブリッドワーク / リモートワーク制度: 業務内容やチームの取り決めに応じた在宅勤務（リモートワーク）とオフィス勤務の柔軟な組み合わせが可能です。
フレックスタイム制度: コアタイムにとらわれない柔軟なスケジュール調整が可能で、育児や介護、個人のプライベートな事情に応じた働き方を尊重しています。
充実した両立支援制度: 産前産後休暇・育児休業（女性の復職率は非常に高く、男性社員の育休取得実績も多数）、復職後の短時間勤務や看護・介護休暇など、ライフステージの変化に寄り添う各種サポートプログラムが整っています。

Salesforce Professional Services is seeking a Technical Architect to help pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical technology customers implement solutions on Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud. This opportunity is suited to Salesforce consultants or developers taking the next step into technical architecture. You will own defined solution components or work-streams with support from experienced architects, progressively building your design and customer advisory skills. Appointment level and responsibilities will reflect relevant experience.

You will work with customers and partners on use cases such as healthcare professional engagement, medical affairs and patient services.   • Experience contributing to technical design reviews, prototypes or customer demonstrations.
  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience.

  • Collaboration: A commitment to shared outcomes, knowledge sharing and the development of others.

The Experience

Do you specialize in systems performance? Do you love working with data and automation? Want to be part of something big? Help build the distributed database technology that powers the growth of the Salesforce Platform worldwide.


SalesforceDB is the transactional database behind Salesforce CRM. It runs more than 1.1 trillion transactions per month on thousands of database instances.


The Salesforce Database team is fast-paced and collaborative. We work across all areas of our distributed transactional database technology stack. We are seeking performance engineers to deliver the tools, analysis, and optimizations that take SalesforceDB to new levels of performance and scalability with every release.


Our performance engineers partner closely with database and storage system developers, application performance engineers, infrastructure engineers, and our analytics team. Together, we deliver all the pieces that add up to high performance in production at scale. Your improvements ship across the whole production fleet every release. Some of our work is published at database research conferences such as CIDR. We are a high-performing team with high standards. We value integrity, rigor, and continuous learning.


What You'll Do


• Drive the design and scalability of our database stack with development teams, from research and conception through delivery in production.

• Find optimization opportunities by profiling the database engine and storage service. Help us meet the performance and scale needs of our largest customers and newly onboarded applications.

• Identify the root cause of performance and scalability problems. Then fix them yourself or drive the fix with the owning team.

• Lead benchmarking and modeling that guide hardware selection and capacity planning for the fleet.

• Build the telemetry, dashboards, and analysis that show how the production fleet performs against its targets.

• Own performance qualification of SalesforceDB releases. Build and run the workloads and benchmarks that decide whether a release goes to production.


You May Be a Great Fit If You Have


• A related technical degree, or equivalent experience.

• 5+ years of performance engineering on systems software, ideally databases, storage, or distributed systems.

• Strong computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, concurrency, and memory management.

• Strong coding skills in Java or C/C++.

• Practical experience with load, benchmark, and regression testing, ideally for multi-tenant workloads at scale.

• A track record of root cause analysis for performance and scalability problems in complex distributed systems.

• Strong SQL and performance data analysis skills (CPU, latency, throughput, per-tenant resource use).

• Experience with telemetry, dashboards, and monitoring against performance targets.

• Fluency with Linux, OS internals, and shell/Python scripting.

• Clear communication and collaboration skills across database, storage, infrastructure, application performance, and analytics teams.

• Integrity and a growth mindset: you report what the data shows, seek feedback, and keep learning.


Additional Qualifications That Could Set You Apart


• MS or PhD in databases or distributed systems.

• Deep knowledge of database internals: optimizer, query execution, storage, transactions, and concurrency control.

• SQL query optimization.

• Splunk or similar log analytics for performance monitoring.

• Java and C/C++ profiling, JVM tuning, and heap dump analysis.

• Statistical analysis and experimental design.

AgentExchange is evolving from a traditional marketplace into an intelligent discovery and distribution platform where humans and AI agents can find, evaluate, and deploy applications, agents, skills, MCP servers, and other capabilities.
We are seeking an experienced Taxonomist & Knowledge Architect to design, govern, and scale the taxonomy and ontology layer that powers AgentExchange. In this role, you will define how autonomous agents, skills, API actions, industry verticals, and data-permission scopes are structured, classified, and discovered, bridging human search intent and machine-actionable metadata while working directly with product managers, search/NLP engineers, and partner ecosystem teams.

Your first priority will be the capability ontology and semantic foundation for our capability reasoning engine. You will plan and deliver this work independently, in close collaboration with Search, Data Science/ML, and Product, and then extend the same foundation to the other taxonomies the platform needs. You will own the development and implementation of the semantic architecture that underpins AI-powered discovery, capability matching, personalized recommendations, and agentic workflows. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in information architecture, knowledge representation, taxonomies, and AI systems with strong product judgment and a track record of delivering scalable platform capabilities.

What You'll Actually Be Doing
Capability Reasoning Engine

  • Define the canonical knowledge model for applications, agents, skills, MCP servers, APIs, and their capabilities, including the taxonomies, metadata schemas, ontologies, and relationships that describe what each capability does, what problems it solves, and how it interacts with others.
  • Model dependencies, prerequisites, compatibility, constraints, and composability across capabilities, and establish how the platform evaluates compatibility and potential combinations.
  • Define the model attributes and relationships that agents use to evaluate whether a solution is trustworthy, compatible, authorized, and appropriate for a given task before recommending or invoking it, in partnership with the reasoning engine team and with Security and Trust for the underlying signals.
  • Define how customer intent, business problems, use cases, and natural-language queries map to available capabilities.
  • Define the controlled vocabularies and facets the engine reasons over, such as industry, cloud, edition, persona, compliance requirements, and deployment type, and describe native Salesforce capabilities and partner capabilities in comparable terms.
  • Co-own ground truth and evaluation with Data Science/ML and Search: labeled intent-to-capability examples, edge cases, and quality definitions for intent-to-capability matching accuracy, recommendation quality, and reasoning correctness.
  • Design explainability and confidence into the model so customers and agents can understand why capabilities are recommended.
  • Enable AI assistants and agents to discover and consume AgentExchange capabilities through APIs, MCP interfaces, and other machine-readable contracts.
  • Partner with Engineering, Data, AI, Design, and Marketplace teams on knowledge graphs, semantic retrieval, reasoning approaches, and agentic discovery, delivering reusable platform capabilities. Write build-ready requirements and versioned schemas for engineers


Taxonomy and Information Architecture

  • Develop extensible semantic structures that accommodate new asset types and evolving agentic ecosystems.
  • Own the information architecture strategy across AgentExchange, including classification, metadata, content relationships, and findability, with consistent standards across first-party and third-party catalogs.
  • Partner with Search, Personalization, and UX teams to improve navigation, filtering, semantic search, and recommendations.
  • Over time, redesign AgentExchange listing metadata to provide structured, consistent, machine-readable descriptions, and define the required metadata for functionality, inputs/outputs, prerequisites, permissions, dependencies, compatibility, limitations, and supported use cases.


Governance and Quality

  • Establish the governance foundation for the knowledge model: a shared glossary, named owners for terms and data sources, decision rights, and source-of-truth indicators at the field level.
  • Establish metadata quality, freshness, completeness, and verification standards, distinguishing publisher-provided claims from independently validated attributes.
  • Define how trust and verification signals are represented in the model and exposed through structured APIs and MCP interfaces, in partnership with Security, Trust, Partner Platform, and Engineering, who own the trust framework. This includes publisher identity, provenance, security assessments, certifications, verified claims, and lifecycle status.
  • Define the definitions, provenance, and refresh rules for outcome and adoption signals such as success rates, effort estimates, and co-install affinity.
  • Develop scalable processes for ontology evolution and catalog consistency without creating unnecessary publishing friction, keeping knowledge models accurate, extensible, and interoperable as the marketplace grows.


Roadmap

  • Own the roadmap for taxonomy development, sequencing the capability reasoning engine first, with discovery with customers, partners, developers, and internal Salesforce product teams.


You’re Our Person If...

  • You have 5+ years of experience in knowledge architecture, information architecture, semantic technologies, or related enterprise platform disciplines.
  • You've built or led products involving taxonomies, ontologies, knowledge graphs, semantic search, recommendation systems, or AI-powered discovery.
  • You have a strong understanding of taxonomy design, metadata modeling, entity relationships, knowledge representation, and information retrieval.
  • You can design faceted classification, where one item belongs to many categories, and model typed relationships beyond broader/narrower links.
  • You've translated complex technical architectures into product strategies, requirements, and measurable outcomes.
  • You have working knowledge of modern AI architectures, including LLMs, RAG, embeddings, and structured reasoning.
  • You’ve worked closely with search, data science, or ML teams, and are comfortable reviewing model or search output and iterating with them.
  • You’re comfortable with SQL, scripting, or notebooks, and with writing requirements against schemas and APIs.
  • You've driven cross-functional initiatives across complex enterprise organizations, collaborating deeply with engineers and architects on technical design decisions without serving as the primary implementation engineer.


Even better If...

  • You have a Master's degree in Library and Information Science (MLIS), Information Architecture, Computational Linguistics, or a related discipline.
  • You've worked with RDF, OWL, SKOS, SHACL, schema.org, or related semantic modeling standards.
  • You've worked with AI agents, MCP, tool discovery, capability registries, or agent orchestration.
  • You've designed taxonomies or knowledge models for large-scale marketplaces, developer platforms, or enterprise software ecosystems.
  • You’ve built taxonomies or knowledge models that fed retrieval or RAG systems.

The Digital Marketing Technology organization powers Salesforce’s global digital presence, serving as “Customer Zero” for our own products — Salesforce, Informatica.com, MulesSoft.com, and Tableau.com — across Content, Identity, and Event experiences. Events Technology is the engine behind Salesforce’s flagship and regional events — including Dreamforce, TrailblazerDX, Tableau Conference, Connections, World Tours, and countless webinars and field events — spanning registration, event marketing, attendee personalization, agenda/session management, badge and check-in systems, live streaming, and post-event video on demand and reporting.

We are seeking a Software Engineering Architect to take on a leadership role for Events Technology. Reporting directly to the VP of Engineering, you will own the architectural strategy and architectural coherence for the event technology ecosystem — from registration and attendee experience through agenda management, event marketing, and on-site/virtual delivery — ensuring these systems operate as a unified, scalable platform that drives event business value at the scale of Dreamforce and beyond.

In this role, you are a strategic partner to Product Leads, Engineering, and Event Marketing. You should have the ability to (if needed) dive deep into code and configuration — prototyping complex flows (e.g., registration and personalization workflows, AgentGraph-driven attendee assistance) and validating architectural decisions through hands-on reference implementations. You will serve as the architectural bridge between Product, Engineering, and event marketing, influencing the roadmap of the Salesforce products we consume by providing high-fidelity feedback based on our internal implementations at event scale.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Horizontal Architectural Strategy for Events Technology. Define and drive the software architecture vision across the events technology portfolio. You will be responsible for ensuring architectural integrity and integration across domains including, but not limited to:
  • Event Platforms: Registration, attendee management, agenda/session builders, badge & check-in, capacity and waitlist management for large-scale events (Dreamforce, TrailblazerDX, World Tours).
  • AI & Agents: Agentforce (Atlas/AgentGraph), conversational agents for attendee support, and digital labor applied to event operations.
  • Data & Identity: Data Cloud (Ingestion/Activation), Identity Resolution, Unified Attendee Profiles, and OAuth2/TBID for event authentication.
  • Marketing & Orchestration: Event Journey Orchestration, Messaging Services (email/SMS/push for event communications), and Transactional Services.
  • Core Platform: Web Application Development for event sites, Headless CMS for event content, Knowledge Graphs, Federated Graphs (GraphQL), and Streaming/ML integrations for real-time event analytics.
  • Strategic Prototyping & Hands-on Leadership. You will validate high-stakes architectural decisions through hands-on prototyping and code-level deep dives. You are expected to build “walking skeleton” implementations of new technologies (e.g., deterministic Agentforce workflows for attendee check-in or session recommendations) to educate leadership on technical choices and set clear patterns for engineering teams to follow, without becoming a bottleneck for critical path delivery — especially given the hard, immovable deadlines of live events.
  • Engineering Multiplier. Shift from individual “hero” delivery to enabling the broader engineering organization. You will empower event engineering teams by establishing architectural standards, conducting design reviews, and resolving cross-team technical blockers ahead of high-traffic event moments (registration launches, keynotes, on-site check-in surges). You will operate as a peer and consensus-builder to architects in adjacent verticals, driving alignment on standards without requiring direct managerial authority.
  • Cross-Pillar & Product Collaboration
  • Product Strategy: Partner with Product Leads across Events, Marketing, and DMT to align technical capabilities with 3-4 quarter event and roadmap calendars.

Must have specific exposure to or understanding of: Data Cloud, Agentforce/AI Agents, Marketing Journey Orchestration, Identity, Content Management, and event/registration platforms.
  • Event Technology Experience: Direct experience with event registration, attendee management, agenda/session tooling, or ticketing platforms — ideally at large scale (thousands to tens of thousands of concurrent attendees) and under fixed, non-negotiable event-date deadlines.
  • Hands-on Proficiency: Ability to read and write code/config when necessary to validate designs. Comfortable spinning up a POC to prove a point or debugging a complex integration issue to unblock a team, particularly under the time pressure of an upcoming event launch.
  • Strategic Influence: Proven ability to influence Product Leads and Engineering Leadership (Directors/VPs). Ability to articulate the trade-offs between “building right” (long-term health) and “building fast” (market and event-date demands).
  • Salesforce Ecosystem: Expert-level understanding of Salesforce platform capabilities, specifically regarding Data Cloud ingestion patterns and Agentforce architectures.
  • Experience in building scalable applications based on micro-service architecture in public cloud infrastructure, able to withstand event-day traffic spikes: AWS components like API Gateway, Lambdas, SNS, SQS, ElastiCache, AppSync etc.

The Experience
Salesforce AI Research is a global leader in Enterprise AI, driving innovations that advance the state of AI while powering enterprise products at worldwide scale.

Our research has helped shape multiple generations of modern AI: we helped pioneer prompt engineering through DecaNLP; introduced BLIP, a foundational breakthrough in multimodal AI; trained state-of-the-art large language models including CodeGen; and pioneered foundation models for time series with Moirai. Today, we continue to advance the frontier of enterprise AI through innovations in AI simulation environments like eVerse, our simulation and agent-training environment; the Atlas Reasoning Engine, which powers Agentforce reasoning capabilities; and other AI systems that are redefining how enterprises reason, plan, and act.

What makes our team unique is our ability to take ideas from research to real-world impact at scale. We work closely with product teams and enterprise customers to translate cutting-edge research into production AI capabilities used by millions of users. Our innovations continue to shape the future of Salesforce products and the broader enterprise AI ecosystem. We also continue to publish at the world's top AI conferences, open source influential research, and collaborate with leading academic institutions. Learn more at Salesforce AI Research.

We are looking for entrepreneurial Research Scientists who want to build, ship, and scale the next generation of Enterprise AI. This is not a traditional research role — you work like a founder within Salesforce, identifying high-impact research directions, prototyping cutting-edge AI capabilities, validating ideas directly with customers, and turning the strongest concepts into production-ready solutions. You have the freedom to propose and incubate new research ideas, access Salesforce's global customer and product ecosystem, and quickly validate new innovations with external and internal customers and stakeholders. We are looking for people who are comfortable with ambiguity, move with urgency, and care as much about customer adoption as technical innovation. If you want the pace and ownership of a startup, combined with the reach and resources of Salesforce, this role offers a unique opportunity to build Enterprise AI with global impact.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Identify research directions with the potential to transform Enterprise AI.
  • Turn promising ideas into zero-to-one AI product prototypes.
  • Work directly with customers to validate needs, test solutions, and refine product direction.
  • Build robust models, agents, and AI systems for real-world enterprise use.
  • Partner with product, engineering, and go-to-market teams to bring solutions to market.


You're Our Person If...

  • You have a strong publication record at top AI venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV, ACL, EMNLP) and/or a proven track record of shipping AI research into real-world products.
  • You have experience with Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or DeepSpeed.
  • You are motivated by real-world impact — you care about seeing your research leave the lab and reach users at scale.
  • You bring demonstrated expertise in one or more core focus areas:
    • Agentic AI and Reasoning: LLM-powered agents, reinforcement learning (RL), reasoning and planning, autonomous workflows, computer use agents, deep research agents, and coding agents.
    • Multimodal and Computer Vision: Vision-language models, video understanding, and multimodal AI agents.
    • Speech Intelligence: Voice intelligence, text-to-speech/automatic speech recognition, and low-latency audio processing.
    • Core Modeling and Post-Training: Pre-training and post-training techniques including RLHF and direct preference optimization, model distillation, evaluation, and time series modeling.
  • You bring a demonstrated ability to conduct independent research and translate ideas into impactful systems.


Even Better If...

title: Technical Architect- Salesforce Devops
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Customer Success

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

The DevOps Architect — Migration Hub is the strategic owner of the CI/CD, environment management and release governance framework that powers all migration wave delivery across the Hub. Sitting at the intersection of platform engineering and delivery operations, this role designs and governs the DevOps infrastructure that enables concurrent migration teams — across Marketing Cloud Next, Agentforce Revenue Management, ITSM and Tableau Next tracks — to deploy, test, validate and release Salesforce configuration, code and data changes at Hub velocity.

Unlike the hands-on DevOps Engineer (who operates day-to-day pipelines within a single track), the DevOps Architect operates at the Hub level — defining branching strategy, environment topology, pipeline standards, test automation frameworks, deployment governance and cross-wave dependency management that apply consistently to every track team.

This role is accountable for ensuring the Hub never becomes a bottleneck — that release pipelines are fast, reliable, auditable and capable of supporting multiple concurrent go-lives within the same programme window.

The DevOps Architect is also responsible for the platform development tooling contribution model — governing how Apex, LWC, Flow and integration code built by track teams is developed, reviewed, tested and promoted through Hub environments to production.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • CI/CD Pipeline Architecture — Hub Standard: Design, build and own the Hub-wide CI/CD pipeline framework using Salesforce DX, GitHub Actions and Gearset/Copado — defining the standard pipeline stages (develop → validate → test → UAT → staging → production) that apply to every migration track, wave and release.
  • Environment Topology Design: Design and manage the Hub environment topology — defining the number, purpose and refresh cadence of Developer, CI, SIT, UAT, Staging and Production environments across all active migration waves, balancing environment costs with delivery velocity requirements.
  • Branching Strategy & Version Control Governance: Define and enforce the Hub-wide Git branching strategy — including branch naming conventions, merge policies, pull request standards, conflict resolution protocols and release tagging — ensuring all Salesforce DX source code, metadata and configuration is correctly version-controlled.
  • Scratch Org Strategy: Design the Hub’s Salesforce DX scratch org usage model — defining scratch org definitions, feature flags, shape parameters and lifecycle policies that enable track teams to develop and test in isolated, reproducible environments at scale.
  • Deployment Governance & Release Management: Own the release management process for all migration wave deployments — defining change freeze windows, deployment sequencing, dependency maps, rollback procedures, approval gates and production deployment runbooks used across all concurrent waves.
  • Test Automation Framework: Design and implement the Hub-wide automated test suite — including Apex test class standards, code coverage requirements, UI automation (LWC Jest, Selenium), data validation scripts and post-deployment smoke tests — integrated into every CI/CD pipeline stage.
  • Static Code Analysis & Quality Gates: Implement and maintain static code analysis tooling (PMD, Salesforce Code Analyser, ESLint) as mandatory quality gates within the Hub pipeline — enforcing Apex best practices, Governor Limit awareness, LWC standards and security vulnerability detection before any code progresses to UAT.
  • Multi-Org & Multi-Track Pipeline Management: Manage the complexity of concurrent multi-org pipelines across 4–5 active migration tracks — designing dependency management, cross-track metadata conflict resolution and coordinated deployment sequencing for shared Salesforce org components.
  • Data Migration Pipeline Integration: Integrate data migration pipeline execution (ETL job scheduling, bulk load sequencing, reconciliation validation) into the Hub CI/CD framework — ensuring data migration jobs are tracked, versioned, automated and auditable alongside metadata deployments.
  • Secrets & Credential Management: Design and enforce secure secrets management for all Hub environments — including connected app credentials, API keys, org authentication certificates, ETL connection credentials and third-party integration tokens using vault-based or CI/CD-native secrets management.
  • Monitoring & Observability: Design the Hub’s deployment monitoring and observability framework — including pipeline run dashboards, deployment success/failure metrics, apex test trend monitoring, environment health checks and post-deployment alert routing for track teams and programme leadership.
  • DevOps Engineer Mentoring & Standards: Act as the technical lead and mentor for DevOps Engineers embedded in each migration track — setting development standards, reviewing pipeline configurations, conducting DevOps design reviews and ensuring consistent tooling adoption across all track teams.
  • Platform Development Contribution: Design and build reusable Salesforce platform components for Hub DevOps tooling — including LWC-based deployment dashboards, Apex utilities for automated org health checks, custom metadata-driven pipeline configuration frameworks and Salesforce Flow automations for release approval workflows.
  • Continuous Improvement — Hub Feedback: Capture DevOps lessons learned after every migration wave — pipeline failures, deployment blockers, environment contention, test coverage gaps
  • Tooling Evaluation & Adoption: Evaluate and recommend new DevOps tooling, Salesforce release management platforms and automation frameworks — maintaining the Hub’s DevOps toolkit at the leading edge of Salesforce delivery practice.



You're Our Person If...

  • Salesforce DX & Source-Driven Development: Expert knowledge of Salesforce DX — scratch org management, SFDX project structure, package development model (unlocked packages, managed packages), metadata API formats and CLI operations for automated deployments.
  • CI/CD Pipeline Engineering: Hands-on expertise building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines for Salesforce deployments — using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps or CircleCI combined with Gearset, Copado or custom SFDX scripting for automated validate-test-deploy workflows.
  • Gearset or Copado: Deep practical experience with at least one enterprise Salesforce release management platform — Gearset or Copado — including pipeline configuration, org comparison, deployment validation, rollback management and test execution integration.
  • Git & Branching Strategy: Expert-level Git proficiency — branching model design (GitFlow, trunk-based, environment-branching), merge policy enforcement, PR review standards, release tagging and conflict resolution for Salesforce metadata and Apex code repositories.
  • Salesforce Environment Management: Proven ability to design and manage multi-org environment topologies for large programme delivery — including sandbox refresh automation, org dependency mapping, data masking for lower environments and environment capacity planning.
  • Apex & Platform Development: Strong Apex development skills — Triggers, Batch Apex, Schedulable classes, test class authoring, Governor Limit management — required for building Hub DevOps tooling, automated health check utilities and deployment validation components.
  • Lightning Web Components & Salesforce Flow: Ability to build LWC-based deployment dashboards, pipeline status monitors, release approval UIs and org health dashboards as internal Hub tooling deployed on the Salesforce platform.
  • Test Automation: Experience designing and implementing automated test frameworks for Salesforce — Apex test class architecture, code coverage reporting, LWC Jest unit tests, Selenium/Playwright UI tests and data validation scripts integrated into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Static Code Analysis & Security Scanning: Hands-on experience with Salesforce Code Analyser, PMD for Apex, ESLint for LWC and SAST tooling integrated into pipeline quality gates — defining and enforcing code quality and security standards across Hub teams.
  • Secrets & Credential Management: Experience with vault-based secrets management (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GitHub Secrets, Azure Key Vault) for securely managing Salesforce connected app credentials, API tokens and ETL integration credentials across Hub environments.
  • Data Migration Pipeline Integration: Understanding of ETL tool scheduling and orchestration — capable of integrating data migration job execution (Informatica, Talend, ADF, MuleSoft) into the Hub CI/CD framework alongside metadata deployments.

title: Sr. Security Governance Engineer - Protect, Detect, & Respond
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About the team


Assurance at Salesforce is being rebuilt as an engineering discipline. Legacy GRC runs on spreadsheets, screenshots, and an annual scramble to prove controls worked months ago. We're replacing it with a model that is continuous, automated, and built into how Salesforce ships. Controls are code. Evidence comes from pipelines, not people chasing tickets.

  • Risk-informed, control managed. We monitor, validate, and improve the controls that stand against threats and failures.
  • Visibility and invention. We give Salesforce a clear, current view of its security posture, and we invest in the people who build it.
  • Always in front. Nothing waits for the next audit to surface.

You'll have real ownership, a real roadmap, and the chance to define what modern assurance looks like for the industry.

What you'll be doing:


As a Sr. Security Governance Engineer, you'll translate enterprise security policies, regulatory requirements, and risk expectations into measurable, technically actionable controls. You'll help build a governance framework where policies and standards are version-controlled, validated, and integrated into engineering workflows. Over time, you'll grow into a Security Control Family Owner for domains such as IAM, Cloud, Application Security, Cryptography, Data Protection, or Infrastructure Security. The focus is governance, control design, and policy ownership. It is not hands-on software development.

  • Policy and standards: Develop and maintain security policies, technical standards, and control requirements. Manage the policy lifecycle: versioning, approvals, exceptions, reviews, and change management. Keep them aligned with architecture, risk appetite, and regulatory obligations.
  • Governance-as-Code / Policy-as-Code: Define structured, machine-readable policy and control requirements. Work with engineering to turn them into guardrails and validation criteria, using tools like OPA/Rego or cloud-native policy frameworks. You won't necessarily own the implementation. Review implementations for alignment with policy intent.
  • Control framework: Maintain a common control framework with clear objectives, ownership, and validation criteria. Establish traceability from regulation to policy to control to implementation. Set expectations for preventive, detective, and compensating controls, and support continuous evaluation of control effectiveness.
  • Control family ownership: Act as the SME and point of contact for your assigned domains. Interpret regulations, assess gaps, exceptions, and emerging risks, and recommend improvements.
  • Collaboration: Work with Security Engineering, Product Security, Cloud Security, IAM, Compliance, Risk, Audit, Legal, and business teams. Bring a governance perspective to architecture and design discussions.

Expected Outcomes

  • Decision speed: Rules are obvious, decisions are fast, and outputs are predictable, with governance built into the engineering workflow.
  • Scalable governance: Policies and control requirements are clear, consistent, and technically actionable.
  • Governance-as-Code adoption: Requirements are version-controlled, traceable, and integrated into security practices.
  • Alignment and visibility: Written policies, technical guardrails, and implemented controls match. Regulations, risks, controls, and evidence are clearly linked.
  • Control family SMEs: Dedicated owners set policy direction and technical standards for each domain.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required — we're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 7+ years in information security governance, security engineering, technology risk, or related functions
  • Strong grasp of security policies, standards, control frameworks, and governance processes
  • Familiarity with NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or PCI DSS
  • Ability to turn regulatory and security requirements into measurable control objectives
  • Working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP), IAM, application, infrastructure, and data security
  • Understanding of control design (preventive and detective), risk assessment, and exception management
  • Familiarity with modern development practices, cloud environments, and CI/CD
  • Strong analytical, communication, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Governance-as-Code or Policy-as-Code, and policy engines such as OPA/Rego or HashiCorp Sentinel
  • Familiarity with YAML, JSON, Git, infrastructure-as-code, and DevSecOps
  • Experience with GRC platforms, Common Controls Frameworks (CCF), and OSCAL
  • Exposure to security posture management, compliance validation, architecture reviews, or AI governance

How We Work:

  • Engineering-first. We use version control, code review, CI/CD, and backlogs. Assurance work ships like software.
  • Automate first. If it's done manually twice, it's a candidate for a build.
  • Signals, not surprises. Gaps become alerts and workflows, and control failures resolve through defined escalation paths.
  • Embedded partners. We work alongside T&P teams as peers, not gatekeepers, and solve problems with them, not at them.
  • Outcomes over activity. We measure risk reduced, effort saved, and audit friction removed.
  • Room to grow. Learn the engineering side if you come from GRC, or the risk side if you come from engineering. We support both paths.

  • Strengthen financial accuracy: Partner with FP&A, Accounting, and Spend Management on accruals, variance analysis, spend closeout, and data quality, ensuring reporting reflects financial performance and timing differences accurately.
  • Advance governance: Develop financial policies, controls, playbooks, and monitoring practices that support consistent execution, compliance, and audit readiness.
  • Drive operational improvement: Simplify workflows, identify system enhancements, improve data integrity, and leverage AI, and automation to strengthen reporting, transparency, operational efficiency, and decision-making.

  • Ability to translate complex financial and operational data into concise executive insights, actionable recommendations, and clear investment tradeoffs.
  • Experience developing financial dashboards, KPIs, and reporting using enterprise financial data, analytics, and AI-powered tools.
  • Proven ability to establish processes, lead change, and deliver results independently in a fast-paced, evolving or ambiguous environment.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trust, guide stakeholders through change, drive financial accountability, and foster adoption of new processes and ways of working.

Even Better If...

  • Experience establishing or scaling a finance operations function within a large, global organization.
  • Familiarity with procurement, purchase orders, project accounting, and the end-to-end spend lifecycle.

  • Scale & Partner Engagement: Design, build, and maintain processes to streamline ISV Partner Launch Onboarding—executing 1:many campaigns across a large partner territory to drive partners through key operational and GTM best practices. Partner 1:1 engagement will be reserved for strategic initiatives across tech adoption, high-potential assessment, and unblocking roadblocks as needed.
  • Portfolio Segmentation & Strategy: Segment & tier a large territory of partners by onboarding stage, potential, and partner type through salesforce reports, and other data tools for targeted campaign execution.

  • Performance Execution: Consistently achieve monthly, quarterly, and annual operational and partner success metrics established by the business.
  • AI & Onboarding Innovation: Evaluate, trial, and integrate cutting-edge AI tools to transform the Partner Experience and scale partner onboarding across a large territory.
  • Foundational Strategy: Help to stand up core processes and documentation for a newly established team function, with the adaptability to refine and expand scope as the role evolves.

  • 5+ years of work experience in sales or partner account management, or partner success.

  • Experience building automation and workflows using agentic tools.
  • Experience with Salesforce reporting, and proficiency segmenting and analyzing data within Excel/Google Sheets.
  • Excitement to work on a new team — loves solving problems and is energized by ambiguity.
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with willingness to develop basic process documentation and partner-facing collateral under guidance.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working on a scaled team, ideally within SaaS, AI, data, or cloud ecosystems.
  • Experience creating enablement and/or email content for external audience.
  • Community management experience.
  • Experience using marketing automation tools.
  • Passion for partner growth and ecosystem success.
  • Familiarity with the Salesforce platform (APIs, workflows, automation, agents), or a strong willingness to learn this quickly.
  • Experience with tools such as Claude, OpenAI, Tableau, Slack/Slackbot, Google Workspace, Workbench.

This dynamic role is pivotal in crafting innovative customer engagement strategies, demonstrating platform capabilities, and translating complex business needs into impactful solutions. You will own the technical strategy for the entire customer life-cycle: from delivering executive level pitches that secure net-new business to maximizing platform adoption that safeguards existing investments.

  • You are a true technophile. You don’t just wait for training, you are already experimenting with the latest in Generative AI, LLMs, and Agentic workflows.
  • Industry Enthusiast. You don’t just understand the manufacturing world, you are passionate about it. You are excited about the opportunity to lead complex digital transformations for the companies that build and move the physical world.

Orchestrate across cross-functional sales, architecture, and solution teams, partnering with clients and internal stakeholders to drive consensus across various Salesforce product lines and align technical deliverables with executive goals.
  • Trusted Advisor & Strategic Roadmaps: Serve as the technical trusted advisor for strategic accounts, navigating a wide array of assignments spanning business development, operations, and IT strategies. Maintain a deep understanding of the customer’s enterprise architecture and understand Salesforce’s footprint within it. Deconstruct ambiguous business challenges and translate them into clear customer journey strategies, scalable IT roadmaps, and actionable next steps, earning and maintaining C-level trust.

Rooted in a true builder identity, you will get hands-on to build compelling tailored use-case demos and transform them into technical agentic pilots. By developing functional LLM-powered agents and AI workflows, you will provide customers with extendable, real-world proof-of-concepts they can actively test and operationalize.

  • Bilingual Proficiency: Fluent in French and English (written and verbal).

Production experience required. Builder mindset non-negotiable.

The FDE SWAT is a hands-on Forward Deployed Engineer role focused on troubleshooting, fixing, and resolving complex issues in live customer deployments. As part of a team of specialists, you will be engaged by FDE Pods or directly by customers when critical problems arise, working quickly to diagnose root causes, implement fixes, and restore stable performance across Agentforce and the wider Salesforce platform. You will own issues end-to-end, from triage and investigation to resolution, validation, and handover, and you will be responsible for clear communication with stakeholders throughout, especially in high-pressure and time-sensitive situations. You will work closely with Product and Engineering as a direct escalation path: reproducing and documenting defects, providing detailed technical evidence, collaborating on fixes and workarounds, and tracking resolutions through to release. The Experience

The Authentication Platform team owns the core identity services for Salesforce's production infrastructure — the Production IAM stack. The portfolio spans Kerberos-based authentication, TOTP, and FIDO2/WebAuthn, bridging legacy infrastructure protocols and modern cloud-native identity standards. Because the platform is a tier-0 dependency for the entire company, we run at massive throughput with a 4+ nines availability target across Public Cloud (AWS/GCP) and hybrid deployments on Kubernetes, with modern CI/CD. Our security posture is Zero Trust and least-privilege by default, and we partner closely with security architects on identity verification and credential-handling design.

You'll work on services in the Production IAM stack as an individual contributor — implementing features across the Kerberos, TOTP, and FIDO2/WebAuthn service portfolio, contributing to designs that senior engineers lead, and taking on-call for a tier-0 platform. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on strong execution, growing technical depth in identity protocols, and shipping high-quality, well-tested code in a security-critical environment.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Deliver features across the Authentication Platform's service portfolio - Kerberos, TOTP, FIDO2/WebAuthn - writing clean, well-tested backend code in Java, Go, or C#.
  • Contribute to design specs and research spikes for features in your area, alongside more senior engineers who lead the design.
  • Implement identity and federation protocols used by the platform, including Kerberos, LDAP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, and TOTP. Familiarity with SAML/OIDC is useful for interop conversations with adjacent teams.
  • Partner with the Product Owner and tech lead on story-level scope, sequencing, and dependencies for your own work, and help refine and clarify work items before they land in a sprint.
  • Reliably deliver as a developer, reviewer, and tester — high test coverage, clean code, and reviews that catch issues before they land, with a security-first mindset appropriate for tier-0 services.
  • Apply Salesforce engineering best practices to code, tests, and CI/CD pipelines. Leave code in better shape than you found it.
  • Use AI development tools (e.g.Claude Code) in your day-to-day workflow, and critically evaluate both human and AI-generated code for correctness, performance, and security compliance.
  • Analyze and fix bugs in your area, working with more senior engineers on the complex ones. Debug production issues and drive them to a fix.
  • Exhibit ownership beyond just coding your features — an active role in testing, review, and monitoring is part of the job, especially given the tier-0 nature of the platform.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for the Authentication Platform and handle common alerts confidently. On-call is a real, high-visibility part of this role because of the platform's tier-0 status.
  • Understand the platform's telemetry — metrics, logs, traces, SLIs — and extend it for the features you own. The availability target is 4+ nines.
  • Contribute to Root Cause Analyses for incidents in your area, and follow through on assigned action items.
  • Work with internal stakeholders — service teams and infrastructure owners who depend on the Authentication Platform — to answer integration questions about the features you own.
  • Author and maintain technical documentation and runbooks for your work.



You're Our Person If...

  • Strong programming ability in Java, Go, or C#, with production experience building backend services.
  • Working knowledge of at least one identity or federation protocol from this set: Kerberos, LDAP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, TOTP, SAML, OIDC. Deeper experience in one or more is a plus.
  • Experience building, deploying, and debugging distributed services in a Public Cloud environment (AWS or GCP) or a hybrid deployment, using Kubernetes and modern CI/CD.
  • Solid grasp of software fundamentals: data structures, testing, code review, source control, CI/CD, and Agile execution as a team member.
  • A security-first mindset — writing code with least-privilege defaults, threat-aware reviews, and thorough automated testing appropriate for identity-critical systems.
  • Ability to debug production issues in a distributed system using logs, metrics, and traces.
  • Comfortable executing an agreed-upon plan largely independently, escalating design-level and cross-cutting decisions to senior engineers.



Even Better If...

  • IAM specialist depth — familiarity with the internals of one or more of Kerberos, LDAP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, TOTP, and the interop story with SAML/OIDC.
  • Security hardening — familiarity with HSMs, PKI, and secure credential storage patterns.
  • Compliance and auditing — exposure to controls and evidence requirements under PCI, SOC 2, or HIPAA.
  • Operational grit — experience on-call for a high-visibility production service, and comfort debugging live incidents under pressure.
  • Experience integrating AI development tools into engineering workflows, including prompt design and reviewing AI-generated code for security-critical systems.



Education

You will identify what is working and what is not, and translate those insights back into practical, scalable governance requirements.


The successful candidate will understand systems and architectures well enough to move beyond validating whether a control exists. They will evaluate how the control is designed, implemented, operated, and scaled across the enterprise.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Support Assurance and Engineering Alignment - Support technical liaison activities between Assurance, Engineering, Product Security, PCLs, and Legal, ensuring governance requirements are clearly understood and actionable.
  • Evaluate Control Implementation - Work directly with Engineering teams to understand how security and compliance controls are implemented within applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud environments, and engineering workflows.
  • Create the Engineering Feedback Loop - Assess what is working, what is creating unnecessary friction, and where controls or requirements are unclear or difficult to operationalize. Feed those insights back into control design, standards, and governance processes.
  • Make Requirements Engineer-Usable - Translate regulatory, compliance, and security expectations into clear, actionable technical requirements that Engineering teams can consistently implement and validate.
  • Develop Second-Line Oversight - Execute second-line oversight protocols that independently monitor, audit, and validate that all security controls are operational across engineering teams in Salesforce (e.g., attestations, CRE checks).
  • Understand Systems End-to-End - Develop a deep understanding of key platforms, architectures, engineering processes, security capabilities, and control implementations to help Assurance make better risk and compliance decisions.
  • Assess Risk in M&A - Assess control and risk exposure during M&As. Design the assessment to price risk, evaluate compatibility, and deliver an executable activation plan tied back to the risk model.
  • Partner on Emerging Security Requirements - Collaborate with Product Security, Legal, PCEs, Market Enablement, and other teams to understand emerging requirements and determine how they should translate into future security controls and engineering expectations.
  • Track the Direction of Compliance Frameworks - Monitor where regulatory and compliance expectations are heading, including AI governance, the EU AI Act, evolving international requirements, and market-specific regulatory expectations. Proactively identify implications for the organization.
  • Support Enablement and Change Management - Contribute to change management efforts, documentation, and training to help engineering teams understand and comply with relevant policies and standards.
  • Support Control Incident Response - Participate in control incident reviews and postmortems, assisting with root-cause analysis and tracking remediation efforts for control failures.
  • Contribute to Control Refinement - Collaborate with control owners to provide feedback on control effectiveness and suggest updates based on operational findings and engineering feedback.
  • Engage Security Champions - Work alongside security and control champions across Engineering to gather feedback, distribute guidance, and support governance adoption.
  • Support Leadership Reporting - Help track and report metrics on control coverage, compliance trends, and risk items to support management reporting.
  • Represent Assurance Requirements - Serve as a point of contact for Assurance in engineering and operational discussions, helping integrate compliance considerations early in development cycles.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required. We're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 2-3 years of relevant experience or technical background in security engineering, cloud security, product security, IAM, platform engineering, or IT governance.
  • Ability to understand complex systems, architectures, APIs, infrastructure, cloud environments, and software development processes.
  • Experience translating security, risk, regulatory, or compliance requirements into technical implementation requirements.
  • Strong understanding of security controls and frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC, SOX, FedRAMP, or similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with emerging technology and regulatory areas such as AI security, AI governance, privacy, and evolving global technology regulations.
  • Ability to work effectively with Engineering while also partnering with Legal, Compliance, Security, Risk, and business stakeholders.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical implementation details to governance teams and translate governance expectations into language Engineering teams can act on.
  • Analytical mindset with the ability to evaluate requirements and provide constructive input based on practical constraints.
  • Experience with independent control testing, assurance or audit practices, incident or root-cause analysis, or M&A due diligence is a plus.

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means creating a strong connection between what Assurance requires and what Engineering can effectively implement. Controls become more technically relevant, and requirements become easier for Engineering teams to consume. Implementation challenges are identified earlier, and emerging security and regulatory expectations are incorporated into the control environment before they become compliance gaps. Control failures are handled with the same rigor as availability incidents, and leadership has clear visibility into control reliability and systemic risk.


Ultimately, this role will help move Assurance from primarily validating compliance to becoming a technical governance partner that actively shapes secure and compliant engineering practices by design.

The Experience:

Salesforce is seeking a proactive, strategic, and high-energy leader to enhance our customer and partner relationships within the Real Estate & Workplace Services (REWS) organization. Reporting to the VP, Business Operations & Strategic Initiatives, this role is dedicated to ensuring that when we engage with external partners, customers, and landlords, we show up as a unified and proactive partner.

You will be the primary orchestrator of our customer engagement, connecting the dots between our subject matter experts, our physical campus, and the Salesforce products that power it. By creating new ways to track engagements and coordinating across internal functions, you will ensure our follow-ups are seamless and our impact on the sales motion is quantified. You will partner closely with our Communications team to help develop and deliver a consistent, high-impact narrative that showcases REWS as the first and best consumer of our own technology.

What you'll Actually Be Doing:

Relationship Orchestration & Engagement

  • Unified Front: Coordinate across account teams and internal REWS functions to ensure we show up with "one voice." You will eliminate silos by ensuring all team members are briefed on history, data points, and previous interactions.
  • SME Coordination: Work successfully across functions (Tech Enablement, Business Ops, Comms, etc.) to ensure the right Subject Matter Experts are engaged for tours, presentations, and high-stakes meetings.
  • External Hosting: Manage external hosting on our campus, ensuring every visit strengthens our strategic relationships with customers, vendors, and landlords.

Customer Zero Storytelling Support

  • Narrative Partnership: Collaborate closely with our Communications and Tech partners to help develop and deliver the "Customer Zero" story, ensuring it highlights Salesforce products that resonate with real estate needs (e.g., Sustainability, Field Service, and AI-enabled tools and innovations).
  • Global Narrative Governance & Standardization: Act as the global gatekeeper for the "Customer Zero" story by establishing a standardized messaging framework and terminology. You will ensure that core narrative pillars remain intact across all global touchpoints—from London to Tokyo to San Francisco—ensuring the Salesforce story remains compelling, credible, and consistent whether delivered by a local site lead or an executive.
  • Proof Points: Utilize real-time metrics from our global office portfolio (including energy savings, ROI on agentified tools, employee experience, facilities management innovations, real estate best practices, and beyond) to provide Sales teams with credible, data-backed evidence that our solutions work.

Operational Tracking & Insight

  • Engagement Tracking: Build and manage new tools and frameworks to track "who, what, and where." This includes maintaining a single source of truth for engagement history, meeting agendas, and discussion topics.
  • Outcome Management: Be the driver of accountability—tracking meeting outcomes and pending action items to ensure no customer request or lead falls through the cracks.
  • Product Feedback Integration: Create a formal mechanism to funnel customer insights from the "field" (the campus) back to Product and Engineering teams, ensuring REWS stays at the forefront of the "Customer Zero" mission.
  • Quantifying Value: Document the time and resources dedicated to sales support to generate impact reports that prove the ROI of REWS participation in the sales motion.

You're Our Person If...

  • Professional Experience: 12+ years of experience in customer engagement, strategic program management, or business operations within a fast-paced corporate environment.
  • Operational Excellence: Highly organized and proactive self-starter with a proven ability to "connect the dots" across complex projects and anticipate business needs without constant direction.
  • Executive Presence & Alignment: Exceptional ability to navigate a matrixed organization and align diverse, high-level stakeholders (Sales, Biz Ops, Comms, Tech) toward a unified strategic goal.
  • Presentation & Communication Skills: Proven experience presenting to customers, external partners, and senior internal stakeholders, with the ability to communicate clearly and engage diverse audiences.
  • Sales Motion Exposure: Base line understanding of the sales lifecycle and experience supporting account teams to drive customer success and strategic growth.
  • Data-Driven Mindset: Proven track record of developing and managing tools or frameworks to track engagement activity, sentiment, and follow-up accountability.

The CSM is responsible for identifying and addressing both technical and business concerns, aligning them strategically with customer priorities, projects, and problems.

We are looking for candidates who have experience supporting customers in one or more of the following industries:

  • Health & Life Sciences (HLS) – Collaborates with healthcare providers, payers, life sciences, pharmaceutical, and medical device companies to support digital health initiatives, regulatory compliance, and improved patient/member outcomes through the Salesforce platform (Direct experience with Health Cloud and/or Life Sciences Cloud strongly preferred).
  • Technology Media Telecommunication (TMT) – Works with technology companies, telecommunications providers, media organizations, and high-tech firms to accelerate innovation, improve customer success outcomes, and drive platform adoption at scale (Direct experience with Media Cloud strongly preferred).

  • Use AI to work effectively: automate routine tasks such as meeting summaries, QBR data collection, and initial health monitoring; use natural-language commands to guide AI agents in retrieving accurate customer data and generating first drafts of success plans; use AI-driven sentiment and intent analysis to flag early customer concerns for human intervention; actively seek out “Agentblazer” training and certifications; prioritize the most urgent work, form a clear plan for client engagements, communicate proactively, keep the customer goal central to decision-making, and apply product knowledge to ask effective diagnosis questions and align platform features with customer priorities and roadmaps.

Experienced business professional, preferably with 3+ years of relevant industry expertise in Customer Success, Salesforce, SaaS platform use, or related fields, including 3-4 years experience supporting customers using Sales Cloud and Service Cloud.

  • Based in San Francisco, Chicago, or Atlanta (Office Flexible, 3 days/week) with up to 25% travel for discovery, kickoffs, and monitoring.

Customers are already running workflows in production; now we’re making that success repeatable across more systems and use cases.


Making computer use dependable raises hard engineering questions. How does an agent know it succeeded? When should it reason, and when should it follow a deterministic path? How should it recover when an application changes or ask for help before making a consequential mistake?


You’ll help answer those questions in production. Our team works directly with customers, building alongside them and turning discoveries into reusable product capabilities. As a Principal Engineer, you’ll remain hands-on while shaping architecture across our agent and backend systems, owning critical capabilities from design through operation, and helping other engineers deliver them.

Drive Agent Development & Architecture

  • Design and build systems that learn from demonstrations and combine AI reasoning with deterministic execution to complete workflows reliably.
  • Develop recovery and verification capabilities so agents can adapt to changes, confirm outcomes, and recognize when human intervention is needed.
  • Build backend services with robust workflow state management, failure handling, and secure access to customer environments.
  • Create evaluations and diagnostics that measure task success, expose regressions, and make failures understandable.

Build Directly With Customers

  • Work alongside customers to understand their workflows, prototype solutions, and validate results in their environments.
  • Investigate where automation succeeds or fails, then turn those findings into improvements to the core product.
  • Help customers move from their first successful workflow toward repeatable, increasingly self-service adoption.
  • Partner with forward-deployed engineers and product management to decide which customer needs should shape the roadmap.

Shape Technical Direction & Grow the Team

  • Lead architectural decisions across agent execution, backend services, and workflow state, aligning system boundaries and tradeoffs with other technical leads.

  • You can reason through concurrency, persistent state, retries, and partial failures in systems that perform consequential actions.
  • You’re proficient in Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • You can turn an unclear customer problem into a bounded technical approach, test it with users, and lead it through production while creating capabilities other engineers can build on.

  • You use AI development tools thoughtfully and take responsibility for the correctness, security, and maintainability of what you ship.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

Slack is seeking a Staff Researcher to help us understand how AI agents are changing the way people work together—and what that means for the future of workplace collaboration.

In this role, you will investigate how people and teams adopt, collaborate with, and delegate work to AI agents. You will explore not only individual experiences with AI, but also how agents affect shared context, coordination, communication, trust, and accountability across teams. Your research will help identify where agents create meaningful value, where they introduce friction or risk, and how Slack can better support collaboration among people and agents.

As a Staff-level individual contributor, you will independently shape and execute a research agenda with a primary focus on Slack's Ecosystem, understanding how AI agents affect the future of workplace collaboration. You will pair foundational research on emerging work practices with practical evaluation of product experiences, translating evidence into clear recommendations that influence product strategy and development. You will also mentor researchers and strengthen how the team conducts and applies research.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Lead research scoping, prioritization, and roadmapping across multiple teams focused on AI agents and workplace collaboration, turning ambiguous questions into focused, actionable research programs.
  • Study real-world workflows to understand how people discover, adopt, delegate to, supervise, and collaborate with agents—and how those behaviors affect team coordination, shared understanding, trust, and accountability.
  • Design and conduct rigorous foundational and evaluative research using a range of qualitative and quantitative methods, balancing depth, speed, and the limits of what each approach can establish.
  • Partner with Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science, and other insights functions to connect customer evidence with product decisions and triangulate findings across studies, behavioral data, and customer feedback.
  • Build compelling narratives and reusable frameworks that synthesize multiple lines of inquiry, identify new product opportunities, and make the user and business consequences of decisions clear.
  • Influence senior stakeholders through practical, evidence-based recommendations; help teams distinguish emerging signals from assumptions and prioritize the most important uncertainties.
  • Mentor colleagues and collaborate with Research Operations to improve research practices, tools, documentation, and the team's ability to deliver high-quality work efficiently.



Minimum Requirements

  • 8+ years of user or product research experience, or equivalent demonstrated experience delivering research at comparable scope and impact. A track record of independently leading ambiguous research across multiple product teams is more important than tenure alone.
  • Expertise in multiple research approaches, with strong qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis skills and sound judgment about methodological trade-offs.
  • Demonstrated experience translating research into product strategy, roadmap priorities, or consequential product decisions in a fast-moving product organization.
  • Strong synthesis, storytelling, and communication skills, including experience partnering with senior stakeholders and creating frameworks that help teams understand and act on evidence.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and mentoring skills, along with working fluency in AI assistants and agents and curiosity about their effects on real workplace behavior. You do not need to be an ML engineer.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Research experience with AI assistants, agents, automation, or human–AI interaction, including questions of delegation, oversight, trust, explainability, or recovery from errors.
  • Experience studying workplace collaboration, enterprise SaaS, knowledge workers, or multi-person and organizational workflows.
  • Experience with longitudinal studies, diary studies, contextual inquiry, or field research that captures how emerging tools become part of everyday work.
  • Experience partnering with Data Science to connect observed behaviors and customer needs with usage data and product evaluation.
  • Experience researching enterprise adoption, administrator needs, governance, or adoption barriers for emerging technologies.



We welcome researchers with a range of professional and educational backgrounds. If you can demonstrate the scope, research judgment, and impact described here, we encourage you to apply even if your experience does not map neatly to every qualification.
